intro: Chang'e 6 landed in the South Pole-Aitken basin on June 1, 2024 — the first sample-return mission from the far side of the Moon, the deepest, oldest, largest impact structure in the inner Solar System. Returned 1,935 g of far-side material to Earth on June 25, 2024 — samples that may contain mantle fragments from the 4.2-billion-year-old basin-forming impact.

images.caption: Chang'e 6 stack — added Queqiao-2 relay for far-side comms, otherwise inheriting Chang'e 5 architecture.
International payloads — ESA NILS detector, French DORN radon detector, Italian INRRI retroreflector, Pakistan ICUBE-Q nanosatellite.
Long March 5 launches Chang'e 6 — 28-day round trip to the lunar far side, including 14 days waiting for the right relay-comms window.
